# Appendix B: Software and reproducibility {#sec-appx-software .appendix}

The software stack is the same as papers 1, 2a and 2b's, described in
full in paper 1's Appendix B: R, the tidyverse, `{DBI}`/`{RMariaDB}` for
the Smartform database, `{renv}` for package pinning, and Quarto for
typesetting, all run as a single reproducible pipeline in which each step
is cached and only rebuilt when its own inputs change. The one addition
here is `{xgboost}`, used directly rather than through
`{tidymodels}`/`{parsnip}`: fitting under a custom objective, a custom
evaluation metric, and race-grouping information together has no
`{parsnip}` interface, the same kind of exception papers 1 and 2 make for
`{mlogit}`.

One part of the pipeline is expensive enough, and consequential enough
for §4's tuning-asymmetry disclosure, to document in its own right: the
grid search behind the selected configuration. The full factorial grid,
before any reduction, also varies `colsample_bytree` over two values —
`r n_144_grid` points under the same five-fold cross-validation, projected
at roughly 12.9 hours, above this project's working limit of about 12
hours for a single run. Fixing `colsample_bytree` at its lower value alone
cut the grid to the `r n_grid_points` points actually run, projected at
roughly 6.5 hours; that was enough, and the further rungs available (also
fixing `subsample`, dropping the lowest `eta`, or narrowing
`min_child_weight`) were not needed. The measured cost came in higher than
projected: cross-validation summed to `r sprintf("%.1f", total_cv_hours)`
hours across the `r n_grid_points` points, meaning the un-reduced grid
would have taken roughly twice as long — the cut was necessary, not a
precaution that turned out unneeded. Most of that time is spent
evaluating the custom objective and its matching evaluation metric, once
each per boosting round: every round needs the gradient/Hessian pair for
the next tree and the held-out score for early stopping, and this
dominates the per-round cost, with building the trees themselves
comparatively cheap.

Two further facts about the search are recorded here because they matter
for anyone re-running or auditing it, rather than for the argument of the
paper itself. No grid point diverged: a guard logs, rather than silently
discards, any configuration whose scores run away during boosting, and it
recorded zero such events across all `r n_grid_points` points. And every
one of the top ten points by fold-mean score
`r if (top10_all_subsample_07) "uses subsample = 0.7" else "does not share one subsample value"`
— not itself part of the paper's argument, but worth recording alongside
the selected configuration for anyone tuning a similar grid on this
objective.
